newsitem.title: USA: PG&E settles dispute over California nuclear plant.
newsitem.headline: PG&E settles dispute over California nuclear plant.

text.p: PG&E Corp.'s Pacific Gas and Electric Co. has agreed to pay millions of dollars to settle an environmental dispute over its Diablo Canyon Nuclear Power plant, a spokesman said Friday.

Jeff Lewis, PG&E's Diablo Canyon spokesman, said he expected the settlement to be filed Tuesday in U.S. District Court in San Francisco. He declined to comment on the amount the company would pay as part of the agreement.

But sources familiar with the deal said PG&E would pay $14 million to settle the legal dispute with state and federal environmental agencies and avoid a lengthy court battle. Half of the money would go to environmental groups.

Federal and state agencies investigated PG&E for two years, and concluded that the company held back data about the potential impact of a cooling system at the 2,200-megawatt Diablo Canyon plant on fish and larvae populations.
The cooling system cycles billions of gallons of seawater through the nuclear plant every day to help run the reactor.
Lewis acknowledged that PG&E withheld some data from regional water quality officials, but he said the company believed the discrepancies had no impact on the environment.
"We don't believe we impacted the environment," said Lewis. "The reason for settling is we want to move out of this dispute and move on."
The Diablo Canyon Nuclear Power Plant, located near San Luis Obispo midway between San Francisco and Los Angeles, provides power to about two million Californians.
